reranked_evidence.title: Farage clippings found in home of man charged with killing Ann Widdecombe - Ynetnews
reranked_evidence.snippet: # Farage clippings found in home of man charged with killing Ann Widdecombe. ## British media say Joshua Kerry, 28, displayed articles about Reform UK and its immigration policies; counterterrorism officers now view the former minister’s killing as a planned, targeted attack. British investigators are increasingly examining a possible political motive in the killing of former minister Ann Widdecombe after newspaper clippings about Nigel Farage and Reform UK were reportedly found displayed on the walls of the suspect’s home. British media reported that the clippings focused on Reform UK, the right-wing party Widdecombe had represented in recent years, and on Farage personally. A source told The Sun that the material included articles about the party’s hard-line immigration policies and suggested that the suspect appeared to harbor a “deep dislike” of the party, its leader and its platform. The discovery is expected to intensify suspicions that Widdecombe’s killing was politically motivated, contrary to the initial police assessment that it may have been a robbery that went wrong.

reranked_evidence.title: Sen. Gary Peters wants ICE to explain why it bought spyware that can covertly take control of phones - CBS News
reranked_evidence.snippet: Nicole Sganga is CBS News' homeland security and justice correspondent. *Washington* — The ranking member of the Senate Homeland Security and Governmental Affairs Committee is demanding that U.S. Immigration and Customs Enforcement explain why it has purchased commercial spyware capable of covertly taking control of phones as well as collecting messages, photographs, location information and other personal data. Democratic Sen. Gary Peters of Michigan called the purchase "one of the most significant expansions of DHS and ICE's surveillance ambitions to date," flagging potential civil liberties concerns and risks to U.S. national security. While the senator from Michigan does not allege that ICE has used Graphite against journalists, protesters or other Americans, Peters demanded the agency disclose whether the software has been deployed domestically, who has been targeted and legal authority supporting use of the tool. Peters also asked ICE for the number of U.S. and non-U.S. people who have been targeted, where they were located and why the software was procured.

reranked_evidence.snippet: April Walker, a San Diego resident, was observing federal immigration agents in a Target parking lot in April when she said they boxed her in and pointed a camera at her face and license plate. It was only reinstated, she said, after she contacted a reporter who then reached out to the Department of Homeland Security to inquire about the revocation. reranked_evidence.title: Congress Rejects Stiffer Penalties For Meddling In IRS Audits - Forbes
reranked_evidence.snippet: The proposed amendment targeted violations of section 7217, which bars the president and other senior officials from directing audits or investigations of particular taxpayers. Republicans on the House Ways and Means Committee voted Tuesday against a proposal that would have significantly increased the criminal penalties for political interference in IRS audits. The amendment, offered by Rep. Brad Schneider (D-Ill.) during a House Ways and Means Committee markup, would have amended tax code section 7217. It’s a little-known provision, enacted in the wake of the Watergate scandal, that prohibits certain executive branch officials from directing the IRS to open or close an audit or investigation involving a particular taxpayer. Congress enacted section 7217 in the aftermath of Watergate in an effort to separate IRS enforcement decisions from political influence. Finally, Congress enacted section 7217, making it a crime for certain Executive Branch officials to request that the IRS initiate—or terminate—an audit or investigation of a particular taxpayer.

reranked_evidence.title: Donald Trump weighs cutting ties with UNCHR as officials urge US to maintain bond - The Jerusalem Post
reranked_evidence.snippet: ## The sources said that the agency had informed supporters that it could be placed on a US blacklist, ending funding, and that Washington could also withdraw from its governing Executive Committee. The Trump administration has in recent weeks weighed cutting ties with the UN refugee agency (UNHCR), prompting a campaign by diplomats and UN officials to persuade the United States to maintain support, sources familiar with the matter told *Reuters*. Eight sources, including diplomats, aid sources and a congressional source, told *Reuters* that Washington, historically UNHCR's largest donor, has been considering disengaging from the agency. They said that the agency had informed supporters that it could be placed on a US blacklist, ending funding, and that Washington could also withdraw from its governing Executive Committee. “People have been alerted by UNHCR to call friends in the administration," a source at an aid group involved in the talks told *Reuters*, saying that many had done so.

reranked_evidence.title: Kashmiri activist Khurram Parvez and journalist Irfan Mehraj freed on bail, under tight curbs - Greenwich Time
reranked_evidence.snippet: NEW DELHI (AP) — A prominent Kashmiri human rights activist and a renowned journalist have been released on bail after years of imprisonment on allegations of financing terrorism in the Indian-controlled portion of Kashmir. Rights activist Khurram Parvez and independent journalist Irfan Mehraj were arrested in 2021 and 2023 respectively, under India's terror laws. Despite their release from a New Delhi jail late Wednesday, both remain under tight court-imposed restrictions as the country’s federal counterterror agency seeks to reverse the ruling. Last week, a lower court in India allowed the two men to be released on bail, but India’s National Investigation Agency appealed the decision. Following their release, the Paris-based International Federation for Human Rights and the World Organization Against Torture said in a statement the two men were arrested on “trumped-up charges.” They also called on Indian authorities to drop all charges against them “as they are part of politically motivated proceedings aimed at discrediting their legitimate work and the JKCCS.”.
